feedback.problem: If $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y,$ use the differential $\text{d}f$ to estimate the change $Δf$ in the value of $f(x,y)$ from $(0,e)$ to $(1,2).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,\text{d}x+\frac{x}{y}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(0,e),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(0,e) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡e\,\text{d}x+\frac{0}{e}\,\text{d}y \\  & =1\,\text{d}x+0\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(0+Δx,e+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈1\,Δx+0\,Δy.
$$

Moving from $(0,e)$ to $(1,2),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =1-0=1, \\ Δy & =2-e.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈1\,Δx+0\,Δy \\  & ≈1\cdot (1)+0\cdot (2-e) \\  & ≈1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $f(x,y)$ increases by approximately $1.$
